entry.summary: Ever wanted to sneak through a maze as a shadowy ninja, dodging guards, grabbing scrolls, and escaping undetected? Let me take you through how I made it, what makes it tick, and how you can play it or even build your own. 🎮 What is Openstate? Sneak past patrolling guards with line-of-sight vision Collect hidden scrolls across a maze Use shadows and bushes to hide Escape through the exit — all without being caught Each level gets harder, and every run is unique thanks to procedural generation. 🎥 Gameplay Demo https://youtu.be/vvg_KIyrTkg 🧠 Key Features 🔁 Procedurally generated levels: New maze every time 🌌 Dynamic guard speed: Increasing challenge each level 📜 Scroll collection for stars 🥷 Crouch, hide, and sneak to survive 🌟 3-star rating system: Based on scrolls collected, exit reached, and stealth success 🔁 Game over + restart system if caught 🛠️ How It Was Built guard.py: AI, patrol logic, detection level.py: Handles maze, scrolls, exit, guards maze_generator.py: DFS-based maze generation ui.py: Timer, star count, detection alerts 💻 Powered by Amazon Q CLI 🧪 Challenges Faced Ensuring maze generation always leads to an exit Getting animations and UI overlays working properly in Pygame 🚀 Try the Game Yourself https://github.com/Kshitij-0007/openstate https://github.com/Kshitij-0007/openstate 🧠 Lessons Learned Simple AI systems can feel very smart with just a cone of vision and patrols Amazon Q CLI can boost productivity and structure — especially for solo devs 🛣️ What’s Next for Openstate? 🧠 Smarter guard AI variations 🧱 Level editor for custom mazes 💾 Save/load progress 🛍️ In-game power-ups like invisibility or speed boost 🙌 Final Thoughts Thanks for reading, and go give it a try! 🔧 Built With: Pygame Amazon Q CLI Canva (video editing) 🕶️ Peace, scrolls, and silent footsteps. Let me know if you'd like a thumbnail image or a post for LinkedIn too. Let's get this ninja everywhere. 🥷💻💥

entry.title: 3KB Cute Animation made in Rive
entry.summary: Hey folks! TL;DR: Rive is a big deal for designers, and developers. I've been experimenting with motion design & micro interactions lately. As context, I'm a full stack dev with a background in design & motion. I've always dreamed about a way to make animations in After Effects that are NOT just meant to be exported as .mp4 files but actual interactive animations I could use on my websites or apps. Back in the day, I messed around with Lottie using the Bodymovin plugin for After Effets in order to achieve that. I'm not gonna lie: it "worked" but it was very bad DX and not really efficient (big JSON animation file). -- 5 years later -- I stumbled upon Rive and started to experiment with it, and wow it's exactly what I would dream about: An animation tool that can export lightweight and interactive animations with full control through code. The export is a .riv binary file that is loaded by the Rive SDK. Starting from that, you can interact with your data bindings and inputs set in Rive in plain JS, enabling infinite possibilities! My personal take is that with the incoming flood of average software due to AI, design delight will be back. And this Rive thing is probably a big deal for the future. Let me know your thoughts! Cheers.
